Yup. They manifest in a variety of colors. I'm partially colorblind, so they look more purple to me, but I'm assured they're sometimes red.

If it helps to describe it; it was the same color (and color movement/ flickering) as you get in a wood fire, when the fire is hot and has burned down to charred logs that are cross-hatched and split by the blistering heat, and the flames dance over them and make them flicker. You know when a log kind of burns down so it is like a sort of grid of charcoal squares that are bright with heat, but the shade/ tone flickers? It looked like that.

I'm partially colorblind, but I think I understand. And, yeah, that's pretty normal.

They come in all sorts of colors. I live at a latitude that experiences them fairly regularly. If I recall correctly, the redish coloring is caused when the charged particles hit oxygen molecules. Oxygen is just one of the many gases in our atmosphere, and it's that variance that causes the different colors.

On a good night, you can see a whole host of colors and shades. There's sometimes a pink that is so bright it looks like neon, and I guess it probably is that way because it's exciting the same particles. My color blindness is mostly in the blue and green parts of the spectrum, but it looks neon pinkish to me.
